System.Title.newValue: Architecture #2: Collapse the formatter family into a render-tree seam

System.Description.newValue:
Collapse the formatter family into a render-tree seam

Recommendation strength: Strong • Dependency category: in-process • Pick order: 2 (after #1)

Problem

IOutputFormatter (src/Twig/Formatters/IOutputFormatter.cs, 25 methods, ~108 LOC) is a wide interface. Each concrete formatter (Human, Json, JsonCompact, Ids, Minimal) re-implements 25 entry points — most of which are stubs or trivial delegations. JsonCompact just delegates to Json. Ids and Minimal stub away most methods. Worse, commands branch on the concrete type (fmt is HumanOutputFormatter) at 11 call sites — a clear signal the interface is not actually doing the work the abstraction claims.

Deletion test: deleting the interface would concentrate complexity into... nothing — each command would just produce a data structure and a renderer would consume it. The interface is shallow; it pretends to be an abstraction but is really a tagged-union dispatch encoded badly.

Solution

Replace the 25-method IOutputFormatter with a render-tree seam:

  • Commands produce a RenderTree (a structured, format-agnostic data tree).
  • A 4-method IRenderer consumes the tree:
    • RenderWorkItem
    • RenderTable
    • RenderTree
    • RenderStatus
  • One renderer per output format (HumanRenderer, JsonRenderer, IdsRenderer, MinimalRenderer).
  • The 11 fmt is HumanOutputFormatter checks become tree-shape decisions made before rendering, not after.

Benefits

  • Locality: adding a new output kind = one new renderer, not editing 25 stubs.
  • Leverage: commands stop knowing about formats. Test commands by inspecting their RenderTree; test renderers by feeding them a tree.
  • Type-checking the structure: render trees are typed; today, "what does FormatSeedReconcileResult actually emit?" requires reading five implementations.

Before → After 

BEFORE (shallow, 25-method interface):
  Command ──→ IOutputFormatter.Format<25 distinct things>(...) ──→ Console
                       (each formatter stubs/delegates 25 ways)

AFTER (deep, 4-method renderer over a data tree):
  Command ──→ produces RenderTree ──→ IRenderer.Render(tree) ──→ Console
                                            (4 methods, one impl per format)

File list (initial cut)

  • src/Twig.Domain/Rendering/RenderTree.cs (new — sum type for nodes: Table, Tree, KeyValueList, Status, …)
  • src/Twig/Rendering/IRenderer.cs (new)
  • src/Twig/Rendering/HumanRenderer.cs (new, replaces HumanOutputFormatter)
  • src/Twig/Rendering/JsonRenderer.cs (new, replaces JsonOutputFormatter + JsonCompactOutputFormatter)
  • src/Twig/Rendering/IdsRenderer.cs (new)
  • src/Twig/Rendering/MinimalRenderer.cs (new)
  • All 25+ command files (refactor to build trees, not call formatter methods)
  • src/Twig/Formatters/ directory (deleted at the end)

Sequencing

Best done after Architecture #1 lands — mutation workflows already centralise the "what to render" decisions, so commands have a cleaner shape to be refactored from.

Acceptance

  • IOutputFormatter is deleted; Formatters/ directory is gone.
  • All 11 fmt is HumanOutputFormatter branches eliminated (grep should return zero hits).
  • Adding tsv (a hypothetical 6th format) requires one new file under Rendering/.
  • All formatter regression tests pass against the new renderer.

Risks

  • Touches many files. Mitigate by introducing RenderTree and one new renderer alongside the old interface, migrating commands one at a time, then deleting the old interface.

System.History.newValue:
Slice 4 complete — JsonRenderer shipped (PR #182, commit 62e9db12)

The seam infrastructure is now complete. Twig.RenderTree ships four renderers covering the full output-format matrix:

  • SpectreNodeRenderer (in src/Twig/Rendering/) — human-format Spectre output
  • JsonRenderer — pretty-printed JSON via Utf8JsonWriter
  • MinimalRenderer — pipe-friendly line-oriented text
  • IdsRenderer — bare integer IDs

Test coverage: 55 passing in Twig.RenderTree.Tests (43 + 12 new for JsonRenderer).

What this slice deliberately did NOT do

No command was migrated to emit a RenderTree. After rubber-duck review of a proposed SetCommand migration, three parity-preservation problems surfaced that each need per-command deliberation, not a generic seam:

  1. Minimal-format byte parity — operator scripts pipe twig set -o minimal expecting #42; generic tree-walking emits a multi-line projection. Each command needs explicit minimal-format projection.
  2. Theme-aware state coloring — HumanOutputFormatter.GetStateColor uses per-state palette knowledge; the generic renderer only knows Severity. Needs either a richer cell type or a renderer extension point.
  3. JSON byte identity — deterministic property order and trailing-newline behavior matters for golden tests; needs per-command projection rules.

Remaining work (out of this slice)

  • Slice 5+: Migrate each command (SetCommand, ShowCommand, WorkspaceCommand, TreeRenderingService, ProcessCommand) — one PR per command, with deliberate parity preservation.
  • Slice 6: Retire IOutputFormatter + delete 5 legacy formatter classes.
  • Add Section.Key field (machine name) before command migration starts.
  • Consider a "command outcome" node variant carrying separate human/minimal/machine projections.

Recommend breaking the remaining command migration work into a child epic so each migration gets its own design pass and PR review.

Leaving #3301 in Doing since command migrations are not yet started.

System.History.newValue:
Slice 6 merged: ProcessCommand on the RenderTree seam

PR #184 — first command to ride the new IRenderer/RenderTree seam end-to-end.

What landed

  • RendererFactory (new): AOT-safe dispatch resolving IRenderer by format alias. Mirrors OutputFormatterFactory's alias map (json/json-full/json-compact, minimal, ids, default human).
  • Binds output sinks at render time, not construction time — necessary for StdoutCapture-based tests that swap Console.Out mid-execution.
  • ProcessCommand rewritten to build Document RenderTrees with DocumentField entries; HumanOverride used so the states/types human output keeps its plain aligned Text shape while machine outputs emit the structured Table.

Verification

  • 24/24 ProcessCommandTests pass
  • 67/67 Twig.RenderTree.Tests pass
  • 14/14 SpectreNodeRendererTests pass
  • AOT build clean, CI green

Pattern is proven; remaining scope

~40 commands still use IOutputFormatter (Show, Workspace, TreeRenderingService, Set, Seed*, Query, Update, Note, Patch, Edit, etc.). Acceptance criteria require all of them migrated plus deletion of the Formatters/ directory. The 3 remaining fmt is HumanOutputFormatter branches live in ShowCommand, WorkspaceCommand, and TreeRenderingService — those are the highest-leverage targets next.

System.History.newValue:
Slice 7 merged: SetCommand on RendererFactory + RenderNode.Markup

PR #185 squashed to main as b994f643.

What landed

  • RenderNode.Markup — new DU variant carrying raw Spectre markup. SpectreNodeRenderer passes through unescaped via MarkupLine; JSON/Minimal/Ids project the markup-stripped string. Enables inline color (e.g. coloured state token in human confirmation) without leaking Spectre concepts elsewhere.
  • MarkupHelpers.StripMarkup — lightweight tag stripper honouring [[/]] literal-bracket escapes. Kept Twig.RenderTree Spectre-Console-free.
  • SetCommand migrated — first command using the canonical per-format-tree-shape pattern:
    • minimal → Text("#{id}")
    • json/jsonc/json-full/ids → Record("setConfirmation", {id,title,state,type})
    • human → Markup(...) with state coloured by severity
    The fmt is HumanOutputFormatter check is gone — tree shape is decided before rendering, exactly as the ticket prescribes.
  • RendererFactory.GetRenderer(format, TextWriter) overload — lets commands route diagnostic output (e.g. interactive disambiguation table) to Console.Error.
  • RendererFactory ctor param made optional (= null, defaulted via ?? new RendererFactory()) — preserves ~20 SetCommand test sites without touching them. Pattern recommended for future widely-referenced commands.

Verification

  • Twig.RenderTree.Tests: 75/75 pass (8 new MarkupRenderingTests)
  • SpectreNodeRendererTests: 16/16 pass (2 new Markup tests)
  • Set* sweep: 130/130 pass
  • ProcessCommandTests (slice 6 regression): 24/24 pass
  • AOT build clean; CI green on PR #185

Remaining scope (deferred per agreed checkpoint)

  • ShowCommand migration — entangled with legacy SpectreRenderer (Live-region two-pass cached→sync→revised, RenderStatusAsync/BuildStatusViewAsync). Full migration requires retiring that interface too.
  • WorkspaceCommand + TreeRenderingService — last two fmt is HumanOutputFormatter sites alongside ShowCommand.
  • ~37 other commands still on IOutputFormatter.
  • Final retirement of IOutputFormatter family and Formatters/ directory.

Pausing here for explicit direction on the next bite.

Slice 9 merged — StateCommand migration

Squashed to main as 211bf203 via PR #187. Third canonical command migration after SetCommand (slice 7) and NoteCommand (slice 8).

Highlights

  • StateCommand routes success / already-in-state / hint output through RendererFactory + per-format RenderTree. Errors stay on legacy FormatError for stderr.
  • New JSON shapes: Record("stateChanged", { id, title, fromState, toState, requestedState, transitionCount, isCategoryResolution, message }) and Record("alreadyInState", { id, state, requestedState, isCategoryResolution, message }).
  • Seed path now routes through the same renderer dispatch as the published path, so machine formats are consistent across seed vs published items.
  • Shape-stability fix: hints are only appended for human output — adding Hint nodes alongside a Record for JSON/ids formats would turn a single-Record document into an array-with-kind discriminator. Worth back-porting to NoteCommand in a follow-up.
  • All legacy message strings preserved verbatim; 36 pre-existing tests pass unchanged + 3 new JSON/minimal tests added.
